content:
In file#Mathlib/FieldTheory/Separable, there is a TODO about generalizing the definition of IsSeparable to allow for transcendental extensions. What we call docs#Algebra.IsSeparable is basically what texts (e.g., Bourbaki and the Stacks Project) would call IsAlgebraicSeparable (docs#Algebra.IsSeparable.isAlgebraic).

In #37934 by @Nailin Guan, there is a definition of possibly transcendental separable extensions. In the PR, it is called IsTranscendentalSeparable, and is defined following the Stacks project by saying that any finitely generated subextension is separately generated (i.e., any finitely generated sub-extension has a transcendence basis for which the remaining algebraic extension is algebraic separable).
The current docs#Algebra.IsSeparable (i.e. IsAlgebraicSeparable) works for any [Algebra R S] where [CommRing R] and [Ring S], not necessarily fields. Using transcendence basis like this will certainly not work in this generality, and will only describe separable.

Bourbaki defines (Alg. Ch. V, §15, Def. 1) separability of a commutative algebra A over a field k as the property that A is geometrically reduced, i.e., if for every extension of the base field, the tensor product is reduced. It seems to me this is a definition that has a better chance to generalize. When dealing with extensions of fields, you this definition will recover what is done in #37934. In fact, the link between #37934 and being geometrically reduced is in the follow-up PR #37838.

Normally, being geometrically reduced is defined only for (commutative) algebras over fields, but in the algebraic geometry folder, this is defined for every morphism from a field to the base (docs#AlgebraicGeometry.GeometricallyReduced).

I think Mathlib should rename Algebra.IsSeparable to Algebra.IsAlgebraicSeparable, and define instead

import Mathlib
open TensorProduct
-- primed to avoid clash with the existing `Algebra.IsSeparable`.
class Algebra.IsSeparable' (k : Type u) (K : Type v) [CommRing k] [Ring K] [Algebra k K] where
  isReduced : ∀ (k' : Type v) [Field k'] [Algebra k k'], IsReduced (k' ⊗[k] K)

Does this seem reasonable as a definition ?
The quantification over Type v is a bit unfortunate. Is there not a more intrinsic characterization of this definition?
It should suffice to quantify over all primes of the base and base change to the algebraic closure of the residue field.
Yeah, I also find this universe shenanigan unfortunate. docs#AlgebraicGeometry.GeometricallyReduced does not have this because both schemes are in the same universe.
But showing this is equivalent is non-trivial (see stacks#030V). IIRC, @Dion Leijnse is working on it.

My suggestion would be to not touch docs#Algebra.IsSeparable and add IsTranscendentalSeparable for now. When we have all the equivalences with geometrically reduced and the characterization in terms of the algebraic closure, we can consider unifying all of them.

It will be much easier to do any refactor if we have all the equivalences available.
(FWIW, the proof of stacks#030V uses stacks#030W, which is in #37838)
Nailin and Dion have coordinated their efforts, so hopefully there should be no duplicated work.
I have the TFAE, I have nothing against change of definition, however I want a notation for this, instead of geometrically reduced for fields.

Christian Merten 发言道：

Nailin and Dion have coordinated their efforts, so hopefully there should be no duplicated work.

I think there is no duplication, I asked whenever I started proving new things. I remember he is on some inseparable stuffs.
I believe the current Algebra.IsSeparable should stay there, about the name, I prefer keeping it there, since for transcendental separable in natural language we also state it defferently.

Thomas Browning 发言道：

The quantification over Type v is a bit unfortunate. Is there not a more intrinsic characterization of this definition?

The algebraic closure is enough for over fields, I can proof it for more general universe using results in #37838 fairly easily.

I still feel the current Algebra.IsSeparable should at least be called Algebra.IsAlgebraicSeparable to avoid confusions.

I had missed that we have docs#Algebra.IsGeometricallyReduced already defined, with that extra bit I think I can be happy with having IsSeparableTranscendental as a special case for fields, and then have theorems linking formally with Algebra.IsGeometricallyReduced.
It would probably be nice to refactor docs#Algebra.IsGeometricallyReduced to work for a general base along the lines of what I suggested above.
I have nothing against this change of name. For link wiith geometrically reduced, I think the TFAE would do the work (:

Naive question: is an algebraic separable extension precisely a transcendental-separable extension that is algebraic? If so, then we should just get rid of docs#Algebra.IsSeparable and prove that theorem.
Relatedly, refactoring name X to name Y and name Y to name Z is painful, so we should move Y to Z early to avoid it.

I am against removing, most of the time we do only care about algebraic ones, this can also be defined over commutative rings.
For unification, I already unified separably generated and transcendental separable in fg case.
isn't Robin's definition above done for a general CommRing?

Artie Khovanov said:

Naive question: is an algebraic separable extension precisely a transcendental-separable extension that is algebraic? If so, then we should just get rid of docs#Algebra.IsSeparable and prove that theorem.

Yes to your question, but the usual definition of transcendental-separable requires the definition of algebraic separable.

Artie Khovanov 发言道：

isn't Robin's definition above done for a general CommRing?

That one isn't ideal enough, currently for geometrically reduced we need it to be over a field.

So, can we have a conclusion now? For the definition itself I don't have much strong preference, but in any case I would like a local abbrev for the current Algebra.IsSeparablyGenerated and Algebra.IsTranscendentalSeparable.

In any sense, I found a bad news: AI found a proof of all extension over perfect field is separable, directly using previous lemmas, this is actually the only reason for me to develop these results. Defeated by AI :sob: :sob: :sob: :sob: :sob:
Of course this result is true by definition, right? Right?
Probably not, it needs every finitely generated extension is separably generated. Algthough this is handled by Andrew earlier using those linear independence of pth power.

Nailin Guan 发言道：

So, can we have a conclusion now? For the definition itself I don't have much strong preference, but in any case I would like a local abbrev for the current Algebra.IsSeparablyGenerated and Algebra.IsTranscendentalSeparable.

Sorry, again, what is our solution?

I guess right now the solution is to keep things like this, and to keep IsTranscendentalSeparable until we have enough to rework IsGeometricallyReduced. I’ve started doing some renaming for IsSeparable to IsAlgebraicSeparable in a branch to free up the IsSeparable name, but I’m not done with that and this is orthogonal for now.

The roadmap is definitely reasonable. Thanks
So what would be enough to rework IsGeometricallyReduced? What would be the key result?

What needs to be done on IsGeometricallyReduced would be that there should be a redefinition to make it works over any rings to mimic what happens in alg. geometry (the definition would be that you remain reduced after base change to the algebraic closure of the residue field at any prime), and then we’d need to show that it is equivalent to the fact that for every extension of ring that is a field, the base change is reduced, and from there what you do in your other PR should be enough to show that for fields IsTranscendentalSeparable is equivalent to IsGeometricallyReduced if I understand correctly.
I think in the coming PR am indeed doing this equivalence, so should we start with refactoring now? Algthough I doesn't have much really depending on it.
Since I proved that for (transcendental) separable extension tensoring with reduced algebra is reduced, I didn't really passed through it. Lets start before more things begin to depend on it.
I refactored IsGeometricallyReduced in #39138. We now have general geometrically reduced algebra over commutative ring is always reduced after base change to arbitrary field in #39141.
